## Scope

Pinned: `base` (efcfb16d) → `HEAD` (07901b22), detached, working tree clean apart from untracked `.skill/`. 9 files, **319 non-test / non-docs lines**, 15 docs, 301 test. Nothing binary, no submodule pointers, no credential-shaped content (`git diff --check` clean, no tabs in added lines, no conflict markers). `.reviews/` written by the tooling run is covered by `.gitignore:31`.

---

## Fix before merge

**1. `scripts/sentry/autofix/sentry-autofix-refused-inventory.mjs:26` — the query hardcodes both label literals and quotes neither, and the failure mode is a silent `0`.**

```js
`q=repo:${repo} is:issue label:sentry-triage label:sentry:fix-refused`,
```

Two things are wrong here, and one edit fixes both.

*Confirmed:* the labels are declared single-source — `FIX_REFUSED_LABEL` at `scripts/sentry/triage/sentry-triage-queue-contract.mjs:191`, `SENTRY_TRIAGE_QUEUE_LABEL` at `scripts/sentry/autofix/sentry-autofix-queue-io.mjs:39` — and every sibling autofix module imports them rather than retyping them (`queue-io.mjs:278`, `family-handled.mjs:144`, `reverse-verify.mjs:222`). This is the only search query in the repo that inlines the strings.

*Unconfirmed:* every one of those siblings also **quotes** the label value — including `label:"sentry-triage"`, which has no colon. This new query is the only unquoted one, and it is the only one whose value *contains* a colon, which is precisely the case GitHub's search syntax requires quoting for. I could not verify GitHub's actual parse: `gh` is disabled in this environment, so no query was sent.

The consequence is what makes it worth fixing blind. If the query is wrong for either reason — a mis-parsed qualifier now, or a label rename later that updates the contract and all importers but not this literal — GitHub returns **200 with `total_count: 0`**. That sails through every gate in `parseRefusedStubInventory`: `validIssueList([], 0)` is `true` at line 51, so the result is `{state:"known", count:0}` and the tracker renders a confident `- Refused stubs (all states): 0`. The fail-closed design catches malformed *responses*; it cannot catch a well-formed response to the wrong *question*. So the one thing this feature exists to surface degrades to a plausible-looking zero rather than `unknown` — on the same tracker where this PR's own docs (`docs/notes/sentry-triage-pipeline.md:1026-1029`) assert five refused stubs await human disposition.

Fix — import and quote, matching `queue-io.mjs:278`:
```js
label:"${SENTRY_TRIAGE_QUEUE_LABEL}" label:"${FIX_REFUSED_LABEL}"
```
No cycle (`queue-io.mjs` does not import `run-record.mjs`). `sentry-autofix-run-record.test.mjs:116` pins the literal query string and needs updating with it.

---

## Follow-up, not blocking

**2. `sentry-autofix-run-record.mjs:67` + `sentry-autofix-finalize.mjs:853` — the `DEFAULT_REPO` fallback is dead; the CLI emits `github.com/null` links.**

`readFlag` returns `null` when a flag is absent (`finalize.mjs:712`), and a JS default parameter fires only on `undefined`. Reproduced:

```
$ node …/sentry-autofix-finalize.mjs run-record … --refused-inventory '{"state":"known","count":2,"issues":[1304,1313]}'
- Refused stubs (all states): 2 ([#1304](https://github.com/null/issues/1304), …)
```

The help text at `finalize.mjs:691` advertises `[--refused-inventory-repo <owner/name>]` as optional; it isn't. **Production is unaffected** — the workflow always passes `REPO: ${{ github.repository }}` (`sentry-autofix.yml:1324`), which is never empty. Fix: `readFlag(args, "--refused-inventory-repo") ?? undefined`, or `repo || REFUSED_INVENTORY_DEFAULT_REPO` at the render site.

**3. `docs/notes/sentry-triage-pipeline.md:1019-1021` — the count can't include this run's own refusals.**

The helper runs at `sentry-autofix.yml:1418`, seconds after the finalize leg applied `sentry:fix-refused`. GitHub's search index is eventually consistent, so freshly-labelled stubs typically won't be in `total_count`. An operator then reads `- Refused (no PR): 1` and `- Refused stubs (all states): 4` in the same comment with no way to tell whether the 1 is inside the 4. The docs present `total_count` as authoritative with no caveat. Remedy is one sentence of doc, not code. Mechanism is documented GitHub behaviour; I could not measure the actual lag here.

---

## Considered and discarded

- **`runGhWithTimeout` (lines 125-231).** Settle-before-kill, SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL, `childDone` guarding the grace timer, `clearKillTimer` on both `close` and `error`. Read against the tests at `run-record.test.mjs:227-278`: no double-settle, no leaked timer. Fine.
- **Adding a line to the run-record body.** The only marker-parsing consumer is the ingest watcher (`alerts/infra/sentry-ingest-watcher/freshness.mjs:15`), which pins `sentry-triage-ingest:run-record:v1` — a different marker from the autofix `sentry-autofix:run-record:v1` (`run-record.mjs:22`). Nothing parses the autofix body's lines.
- **Suite-gate manifest.** The new module is a non-test module reached through `run-record.test.mjs`'s import closure, so `findSentrySuites()` set equality is unaffected and the isolation snapshot covers the `readFileSync` line-cap test. Ran `sentry-suite-gate.mjs`: 14 suites ran and asserted, all ok.
- **`validIssueList`'s `length === min(count, 10)`** against `per_page=10` — correct for page 1, including `total_count > 10`.
- **Floor drift** in `sentry-suite-manifest.json` (run-record 7 vs 23 passing; finalize 44 vs 65) — pre-existing, and explicitly excused by the manifest's own readme.
- **Docs 1023-1029**, the historical-attribution paragraph, asserts operator behaviour (two `workflow_dispatch` runs, manual label removal). Not checkable from the repo; left unverified rather than reported.

## What I could not do

- **`scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh` never ran** — `js-yaml` is missing from `node_modules`, so `scripts/gate/lockfile-scope.mjs` fails to import. The new routing assertions at `agent-quality-gate.test.sh:4415-4419` are read-verified only. The `case` pattern at `agent-quality-gate.sh:4091` does contain the new path.
- **Second-model leg was degraded, not clean.** `codex-review.sh base` ran to completion but wrote a **0-byte** report (`.reviews/codex-review-20260827-204134.md`, no `latest.md` mirror). Only the streamed summary survived. It independently reproduced finding #2 and surfaced nothing else — it did not engage with the query construction at all. Treat it as partial coverage, not corroboration of the clean parts.
- `gh` is disabled here, so no request reached GitHub. That is exactly why #1 is unresolved.

## Proof still owed

- One real `gh api search/issues` with line 26's query, compared against the quoted form — settles #1 in a single command.
- `pnpm agent:quality-gate` after a full `pnpm install`.
- Nothing here proves the new step runs in CI. `record-run` is `continue-on-error: true` (`sentry-autofix.yml:1320`), so a failure of this helper never reds the run — it surfaces only as `unknown` on #1282.

## Verdict

**Does not pass as-is.** One blocker (#1, confirmed as a single-source violation; the quoting risk rides on the same one-line fix), one non-blocking CLI defect (#2), one doc caveat (#3). Green suites here cover the module in isolation — they do not cover whether the query returns the right rows, which is the whole point of the feature.

Want me to apply #1 and #2? Both are contained edits plus the pinned query string in `run-record.test.mjs:116`.
other_review:
The production workflow supplies the repository flag, but the documented optional CLI path emits invalid issue links when it is omitted. The patch also adds volatile incident status to a canonical operator runbook.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Apply the default repo when the CLI flag is omitted — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1984-07901b22c0da/scripts/sentry/autofix/sentry-autofix-finalize.mjs:853-853
  When `run-record` receives a known `--refused-inventory` but omits the optional `--refused-inventory-repo`, `readFlag` returns `null`. Passing that value overrides the renderer's default parameter and produces links such as `https://github.com/null/issues/1304`. Coalesce the missing flag to `undefined` or the default repository before rendering.

- [P2] Keep live refusal status out of the canonical runbook — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1984-07901b22c0da/docs/notes/sentry-triage-pipeline.md:1030-1031
  This finite five-issue disposition list is live work status in a `canonical: true` operator runbook. It becomes false when a disposition lands or the issue closes, while this runbook explicitly routes current state to tracker #1282 (`docs/notes/sentry-triage-pipeline.md:21-24`). Move this status to the tracker and retain only lasting workflow behavior here, as required by `docs/context-standards.md:125-127`.
